note: Level 1, both label levels read (.sav copied from the batch_646 wallace_2026_cengage cache; sha256 matches the batch_645-655 records; Study 2 .sps sha256 9cffe822...4f3ec, contains no engage text). CODE DERIVATION: SINGLE spec s2_engage.csv = (s2, engage{i} -> engage{i}, i = 1,2), no flip, so item IS the source column name: exempt from Step 5b, no verification files. Study 2 only (live has no cov_study and no itemcov_recoded column). Variable labels: engage1 = I would feel engaged by this course., engage2 = I would find this course motivating. -- shipped verbatim, unprefixed (single study). OPTIONS: both items value-labelled 1=1 - Strongly agree, 2..6 bare digits, 7=7 - Strongly disagree; shipped Strongly agree / Strongly disagree with the number prefixes stripped (sibling convention), 2-6 blank, not padded. Sanity counts (not required for the exemption): source 838 rows, 838 non-missing on each item; live 1676 rows = 838 ids x 2; study x item resp-count vectors source = live exactly: engage1 88/102/124/174/163/91/96, engage2 101/109/129/141/124/112/122; every item used all 7 levels. Direction cross-check: engage mean correlates -0.60 with the Study 2 interest mean (interest1-3, labelled 1 = not at all ... 7 = extremely) and +0.67 with the like1-2 mean (1 = Strongly agree), r(engage1, engage2) = +0.86, so the printed 1 = Strongly agree direction is consistent with the data; high resp = LESS engagement, as the build script docstring states. No instructions or lead-in text in the .sav or .sps; instructions left blank. The course referred to is the one taught by the professor whose mindset was manipulated (per the Study 2 sibling labels, e.g. interest1 How interested would you be in taking a class taught by the professor?); not written into item_text. Rights: study-authored items; no fee, permission, NC or redistribution clause located (silence = permission). Not in instrument_rights_register.csv; no register row written.
public_note: Responses run 1 = Strongly agree to 7 = Strongly disagree, so a higher value means less anticipated engagement in the professor's course.
